The api died because the disk filled up: a `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB to `/var/lib/stockroom` in eight minutes, Postgres ran out of space, and the api exited and never came back.

One thing to check first: every timestamp in this log is from 2026-03-09, not last night. If the outage you mean was 3 October, this is the wrong or a stale log file — though the same failure may well have recurred.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–03:05 | Normal traffic, all 200s. |
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing 512 MB CSV parts to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds. |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export part written (40 parts in total). |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 onward | `ERROR proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes, 68 times, still going at 05:28. |

- **Duration:** the api logs no requests after 03:14 and was still down when the log ends at 05:29:57, so at least 2 h 16 min. The log shows no restart attempt, even though compose has `restart: unless-stopped` on the api.
- **Other services:** `web` and `proxy` kept logging 200s throughout.
- **Unrelated noise:** the 43 `cache: slow command` warnings (100–147 ms) run all night at a steady rate, before and after the crash.
- **Root cause:** the exports and the database share one volume, and nothing acted on the 91% warning in the five minutes before it filled.
- **Not in this repo:** I can't find the `report-export` job under `scripts/` or `app/`, so I can't say why it wrote so much or what stopped it at 03:12:48.

I changed nothing. To recover, free space under `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` and start the api; to prevent a repeat, move exports off the database volume or cap the job.

Separately, the ponytail plugin has a statusline badge that isn't configured yet — say so if you want me to add it to `settings.json`.
